artifact: Issue #9 M3-A3 revision / CAS / transaction / concurrency design freeze (design-only)

revision_model.selection_rationale: A1 defines the Subject as the durable identity anchor and mechanical lifecycle carrier of exactly one unit of work, with Execution/Completion/Decision records owned by exactly one Subject and Subject mechanical state transitions revisioned. The durable subject graph regressions (B011/B013/B014/BIND-1/ACTIVATE-R-current-binding/RECOVERY-1) all refer to the Subject as the durable unit. Revisioning at the Subject aggregate therefore aligns the concurrency unit with the ownership and lifecycle unit defined by A1, keeps independent Subjects concurrently mutable (LOST_UPDATE_ALLOWED=no without global serialization), and gives every multi-record write under one Subject a single atomic revision point. One deliberate exception keeps A1 Workflow revision_participation=yes without coupling Subjects: Workflow's own mutable record fields revision under an independent Workflow-record revision scope (revision_scope). This is a deliberate primary/hybrid boundary, not storage convenience.

evaluated_alternatives.revision_unit: one revision for the entire durable subject graph
reasons: any mutation would advance a single global revision, so every independent Subject's CAS read would be invalidated by any other Subject's commit (spurious contention)
requires global serialization of independent Subjects, which the A3 contract explicitly rejects as non-canonical
a single global revision makes the graph one giant aggregate, contradicting A1 aggregate ownership (Subject owns its Executions/Decisions)
no storage-free canonical representation survives whole-graph coupling; recovery/projection rebuild would require whole-graph replay

evaluated_alternatives.revision_unit: one revision per Workflow (its WorkSubjects and records)
reasons: A1: Workflow is a durable record of semantic intent shared 0..n by WorkSubjects and carries no mechanical lifecycle state
two independent child Subjects of the same Workflow would spuriously conflict on one Workflow revision
Workflow identity is stable across revisions; Plan document revisions are revisioned records/decisions, not Workflow mutations

the rejected model is a Workflow-WIDE revision of its WorkSubjects; it is distinct from the selected independent Workflow-RECORD scope for Workflow's own mutable fields, which is not a Workflow-wide revision and never serializes WorkSubjects

evaluated_alternatives.revision_unit: every record carries its own independent revision
reasons: cannot express multi-record atomicity: a child Subject, its initial state and its FollowupEdge(s) must commit as one unit (no orphan child, no edge without child)
Execution mechanical_status and Completion must transition together (terminal transition), which record-level revisions cannot make atomic
append-only records (Completion/Decision/FollowupEdge) would each need a counter, and no record carries the aggregate CAS authority

evaluated_alternatives.revision_unit: Subject aggregate for single-root mutations plus a two-root commit for followup creation
reasons: the only cross-Subject commit in A3 scope is parent -> new-child followup creation (child does not pre-exist, so only the parent side can race)
hybrid is not a third revision unit: the two roots keep their own revision counters; the followup commit is an atomic two-root transaction, not a new aggregate
all other cross-existing-Subject transactions are minimized and deferred (multi_subject_policy)

revision_ownership.revision_choreography_rule: revision numbering, ordering, and expected/current resolution are mechanical control-plane concerns: the expected revision for any mutation is resolved by the authority/lease control plane mechanically reading the canonical current revision of the target aggregate from the durable record set; the model never supplies, orders, or selects revision numbers, and no model input can override the mechanical resolution
revision_ownership.expected_revision_resolution: expected_revision is resolved mechanically by the control plane at lease issuance (read of the target aggregate's current canonical revision from the durable record set) and re-validated at the pre-commit CAS check

revision_scope.exception_rationale: A1 canonical_records.Workflow declares revision_participation=yes (every mutation is a revision; immutable core fields never mutate in place) and mutable_fields scope_annotations/non_semantic_metadata. To honor A1 without serializing WorkSubjects, Workflow's own mutable fields revision under an independent Workflow-record revision scope when/if the operation that mutates them exists. This is a deliberate primary/hybrid boundary chosen on ownership and lifecycle grounds (Subject aggregate owns Subject lifecycle and lineage; Workflow is a shared intent record with no lifecycle), not storage convenience.

revision_increment_rule.rule: explicit increment semantics: which operations advance which revision scope, and how
increments_subject_aggregate: parent FollowupEdge / child creation (followup transaction: parent aggregate advances, child aggregate initializes at rev 1)
revision_increment_rule.append_only_rule: append-only records (Completion, Decision, FollowupEdge) advance the owning Subject aggregate revision at commit; they carry no later mutation and no later revision change
revision_increment_rule.child_initial_rule: a new child Subject starts at its own independent revision 1 (revision_number 1 of its own aggregate, own token)
revision_increment_rule.workflow_mutable_fields_rule: if/when an operation mutates Workflow scope_annotations/non_semantic_metadata, that mutation advances the independent Workflow-record revision scope only; it never advances any Subject aggregate and never serializes WorkSubjects
revision_increment_rule.workflow_immutable_core_rule: Workflow immutable core fields (workflow_id, semantic_intent, goal, scope, context_references, creation_context) never mutate in place (A1), so no revision increment exists for them

revision_representation.revision_type: an opaque content-derived revision_token paired with a monotonic revision_number per aggregate; this is the canonical storage-independent revision type - no database, storage engine, or serialization format is selected (NO_STORAGE_ENGINE_FROZEN=yes)
revision_representation.aggregate_id: canonical Subject internal ID (minted or deterministic per A1 subject_identity_rule); the revision unit is identified by the Subject aggregate, never by executor, session, path, or pointer
revision_representation.revision_number: monotonically increasing integer >= 1 within the aggregate, never reused, no gaps required; the initial revision of any Subject is revision_number 1 (child Subjects start at their own independent revision 1)
revision_representation.revision_token: opaque content-derived token: deterministic hash over the aggregate's committed record set plus the previous revision_token (chain) or the initial token for revision 1
revision_representation.storage_independent: the representation is defined by the contract, not by any storage engine: any storage mapping must expose exactly this canonical revision unit, counter and token; NO_STORAGE_ENGINE_FROZEN=yes
revision_representation.ordering_semantics: revision_number strictly increases on every committed mutation; revision_token changes if and only if the committed record set changed; equal token implies identical committed record set
revision_representation.no_choreography: the model defines the revision contract but does not choreograph revision: no lock manager, no revision coordinator, no storage-specific revision table is defined by M3-A3

workflow_revision.rule: no Workflow-wide revision is required for ordinary cross-Subject operations: Workflow is a durable intent record shared 0..n by WorkSubjects and carries no mechanical lifecycle; a Workflow-wide revision would couple independent children of one Workflow and is rejected. Workflow's own mutable record fields (scope_annotations, non_semantic_metadata) revision under an independent Workflow-record revision scope when/if that operation exists (A1 Workflow revision_participation=yes preserved). Workflow revision never serializes all WorkSubjects.
workflow_revision.rationale: A1 canonical_records.Workflow revision_participation=yes is honored through the independent Workflow-record scope, keeping Subject aggregates as the PRIMARY concurrency/revision boundary; ordinary cross-Subject operations never read or CAS a Workflow revision, and Workflow revision never serializes all WorkSubjects.

records_sharing_revision.Subject_root: yes (mechanical_state transitions advance the aggregate revision)
records_sharing_revision.Execution: yes (mechanical_status changes, including terminal transition, advance the owning Subject aggregate revision)
records_sharing_revision.Completion: yes (append-only; a Completion is committed as part of the owning Subject aggregate and advances its revision)
records_sharing_revision.Decision: yes (append-only; a Decision is committed as part of the owning Subject aggregate and advances its revision)
records_sharing_revision.FollowupEdge: attached_at_creation (an edge created with a child Subject commits in the same unit as the child's initial revision and advances the parent aggregate revision; edges are append-only and never mutate later)
records_sharing_revision.ParentChildEdge: same as FollowupEdge (alias per A1); no separate revision identity
records_sharing_revision.Workflow: independent Workflow-record revision scope for its own mutable fields only (scope_annotations, non_semantic_metadata); never part of any Subject aggregate; no Workflow-wide revision for ordinary cross-Subject operations

parent_child_creation_atomicity.rule: parent -> new-child creation commits as a single two-root atomic unit: child Subject initial revision (rev 1) + at least one FollowupEdge + mechanically verified source Decision basis become visible together or not at all

child_initial_revision.rule: the child Subject gets its own independent initial revision (revision_number 1 of its own aggregate); it does not inherit the parent's revision number or token

aggregate_boundary.aggregate_definition: The Subject aggregate is the root of the revision unit: Subject root record plus every Execution, Completion and Decision owned by that Subject (exactly-one ownership per A1), plus FollowupEdges for which the Subject is parent or child. The aggregate boundary is the A1 ownership boundary: ownership is never transferred by executor or current pointers.
aggregate_boundary.single_root_transactions: Every mutation that touches only records of one Subject aggregate commits as one single-root transaction against that aggregate's revision (CAS on the aggregate revision token).
aggregate_boundary.two_root_transaction_shape: Followup creation (parent Subject + new child Subject) is the only canonical two-root transaction in A3 scope; it commits atomically and advances both roots' revisions (see followup_transaction).
aggregate_boundary.workflow_outside_aggregate: Workflow is not part of any Subject aggregate; it is referenced by Subjects and carries an independent Workflow-record revision scope for its own mutable fields (see revision_model.workflow_revision); no Subject aggregate ever CASes a Workflow revision.
aggregate_boundary.edge_attachment: FollowupEdge records are append-only; their revision participation is fixed at creation (child side at child initial revision; parent side at parent revision advancing with the edge). No later mutation of an edge exists, so no edge-revision conflict is representable.
aggregate_boundary.no_aggregate_transfer: A record never migrates between aggregates; aggregate membership is fixed by A1 ownership (subject_ref / execution_ref / source_decision_ref).

cas_model.definition: Compare-and-set is the canonical concurrency primitive for authoritative mutation: a mutation carries the expected_revision of its target aggregate; the commit succeeds only if the current revision token of the target aggregate still equals the expected token at the pre-commit check; on success the aggregate advances to a new revision token.
cas_model.expected_revision: the canonical revision token (and revision_number) of the target aggregate as validated when the mutation was prepared and as bound in the capability lease (LEASE_REVISION_BOUND)
cas_model.current_revision: the canonical revision token of the target aggregate at pre-commit check time, read from the durable authoritative record set (not from any projection, cache, pointer, or event log)
cas_model.pre_commit_check: expected token == current token; equal commits (new token derived from the committed record set), unequal fails closed with REVISION_CONFLICT; no merging, no last-write-wins, no lost update
cas_model.retry_rule: a REVISION_CONFLICT retry must re-read the current revision and re-validate all authority facts (fresh lease with the new expected revision, fresh authority evaluation); blind retry with stale facts is denied

no_bypass_except.rule: The ONLY defined exceptions to CAS-before-commit are the M3-A4 bootstrap (initial authoritative population of the graph from authoritative bootstrap inputs, where no concurrent authoritative mutation can exist by construction) and the M3-A4 cutover (explicitly recorded transition replacing legacy current_* authority with derived projections). Any such bypass must be recorded by the M3-A4 lane, is never a normal mutation path, and is not usable for ordinary mutations.

cas_model.model_does_not_choreograph_detail: M3-A3 defines expected/current semantics, the pre-commit check, failure behavior and exception boundaries only. It defines no lock manager, no revision coordinator, no storage-specific CAS engine, no distributed consensus, and no runtime behavior.
cas_model.authoritative_read: the current revision used by CAS is read from the durable authoritative record set; Event Log, git history, control comments, current_* pointers and projections are never CAS sources (EVENT_LOG_IS_SUBJECT_AUTHORITY=no, CURRENT_POINTERS_ARE_AUTHORITY=no)

lease_revision_contract.typed_target_binding: the lease object_ref is a typed object reference with object_kind=Subject and object_id equal to the canonical Subject internal ID (A12 rule A); possessing a bare Subject ID is never authority; raw internal IDs are never normal model input (A2)
lease_revision_contract.expected_revision_bound: the lease binds the exact expected revision (canonical revision token + revision_number) of the typed target aggregate at issuance
lease_revision_contract.operation_and_scope_bound: operation (contract identity) and mutation_scope are bound per A2; scope expansion denied
lease_revision_contract.consumption_rule: at consumption the authority engine verifies principal, operation, typed object_ref, mutation_scope, lease validity/current time, AND that the lease expected_revision equals the current revision token of the target aggregate
lease_revision_contract.stale_unexpired_rule: a lease that is not expired but whose expected_revision no longer equals the current revision of the target aggregate is denied (REVISION_MISMATCH per A2 error semantics): staleness is a hard denial independent of expiry, so an unexpired lease can never mutate a stale target
lease_revision_contract.stale_lease_revision_mutation_rule: any mutation attempted with a lease whose expected_revision differs from the target aggregate's current revision is denied (STALE_LEASE_REVISION_MUTATION=denied); no operation-dependent exception is granted
lease_revision_contract.reissue_after_revision_change_rule: after any committed revision change of the target aggregate, an outstanding lease is stale and must be replaced: LEASE_REISSUE_REQUIRED_AFTER_REVISION_CHANGE=yes — a fresh lease with the new expected_revision must be issued through the A2 issuance rules; the old lease is never repaired, renewed, or revalidated against the new revision
lease_revision_contract.expiry_hard_denial: now >= expires_at is a hard denial (LEASE_EXPIRED); LEASE_EXPIRY_ENFORCED=yes
lease_revision_contract.expiry_cannot_expand_authority: lease expiry can never silently expand authority: denial on expiry is hard and final for that lease; no implicit renewal, expansion, or substitution (A2); a fresh lease must be issued through issuance rules
lease_revision_contract.semantic_boundary: the lease is mechanical evidence only; the authority engine mechanically verifies facts, never reasons semantically (AUTHORITY_ENGINE_PERFORMS_SEMANTIC_REASONING=no)

transaction_boundary.authoritative_transaction: the single commit unit that changes the durable authoritative record set of one Subject aggregate (or the canonical followup two-root unit). Only the authoritative transaction is a CAS commit; it is the only place where revision advances.
transaction_boundary.post_commit_projection: projections (current decision, current plan, current followup, binding 0/1/many) are derived deterministically AFTER the authoritative commit, are rebuildable, and are never part of the transaction (CURRENT_POINTERS_ARE_AUTHORITY=no; CURRENT_POINTERS_ARE_PROJECTIONS=yes)
transaction_boundary.post_commit_audit: audit records are written AFTER the authoritative commit and are evidence, never a second authoritative write (DUAL_AUTHORITATIVE_WRITE=no)
transaction_boundary.separation_rule: no projection write and no audit write participates in the authoritative transaction, and no authoritative commit depends on projection/audit success (AUDIT_FAILURE_ROLLS_BACK=no)
AUTHORITATIVE_TRANSACTION_CONTENTS: followup verification + edge + child creation (when the transaction is a followup transaction)
mechanical Subject state transition and the resulting revision update
atomic idempotency reservation and outcome metadata
POST_COMMIT_PROJECTION_CONTENTS: derived current decision projections (latest record per decision_kind)
any other read-model derivation over the committed durable record set
transaction_boundary.idempotency_metadata_relation: idempotency reservation and outcome metadata commit ATOMICALLY WITH the authoritative transaction as durable dedupe metadata; it is NOT graph authority: it never authorizes, never selects, never binds, never participates in projections, and never appears in derived current state
transaction_boundary.projection_failure_rationale: the durable authoritative record set is the only authority; projections are derived and rebuildable (CURRENT_POINTERS_ARE_PROJECTIONS=yes), so a projection publication failure must never roll back or block a canonical commit; post-commit projection is eventually consistent with the durable record set and projection lag is permitted
transaction_boundary.transaction_scope_default: one transaction = one Subject aggregate (single root)
transaction_boundary.cross_subject_scope: only the followup creation shape (parent + new child) is a canonical cross-Subject transaction in A3 scope; all other cross-existing-Subject transactions are minimized and deferred (multi_subject_policy)
transaction_boundary.no_whole_graph_transaction: no transaction spans the whole graph; no transaction couples unrelated Subjects
transaction_boundary.no_operation_level_transaction: no transaction spans multiple operations unless they touch exactly one aggregate

followup_transaction.definition: the canonical two-root authoritative transaction that creates a child Subject from a parent Subject on the basis of an already-materialized Decision (LLM_or_user_materialized_decision)
commit_unit: child Subject record with its own independent initial revision (revision_number 1)
at least one FollowupEdge (parent_subject_ref, child_subject_ref, source_decision_ref)

mechanical verification that the source Decision exists, is owned by the parent Subject, and is already materialized (AUTHORITY_ENGINE_MAY_VERIFY_MATERIALIZED_DECISION=yes; the engine verifies, never infers intent and never creates the Decision)
followup_transaction.orphan_child_rule: a child Subject without at least one FollowupEdge is forbidden: child creation and its >=1 parent edge commit in the same unit
followup_transaction.edge_without_child_rule: a FollowupEdge referencing a child Subject that does not exist is forbidden: edge and child commit together
followup_transaction.child_without_decision_rule: a child Subject whose source_decision_ref does not reference an existing, parent-owned, materialized Decision is forbidden; the authority engine mechanically verifies the Decision basis and never performs semantic reasoning
followup_transaction.atomicity_rule: the followup transaction commits atomically: no observer ever sees the child without its edges, an edge without its child, or a child whose Decision basis failed verification; a crash before commit leaves nothing, a crash after commit leaves the full unit (crash_atomicity)
followup_transaction.parent_cas_before_commit: the followup transaction CASes the parent Subject aggregate expected_revision before commit; if the parent moved, the whole transaction fails closed (REVISION_CONFLICT when nothing was prepared; TRANSACTION_CONFLICT when the child side was already prepared) and no partial effect is visible
followup_transaction.parent_revision_increment: on commit the parent aggregate revision advances (outgoing edge(s) and optional mechanical state transition) in the same atomic unit
followup_transaction.child_revision_independent: the child's initial revision is independent of the parent's revision sequence (child aggregate revision 1, own counter and token)
followup_transaction.verified_materialized_decision: the source Decision is mechanically verified before commit: it exists, is owned by the parent Subject, and is already materialized (LLM_or_user_materialized_decision); the engine verifies only and never infers intent or creates the Decision (AUTHORITY_ENGINE_MAY_VERIFY_MATERIALIZED_DECISION=yes)
followup_transaction.edge_child_atomicity: edge(s) and child commit atomically: the child's initial revision and at least one FollowupEdge become visible together or not at all
followup_transaction.duplicate_child_effect: replay of a followup transaction after an uncertain commit must not create a second child (idempotency_model; IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY=must_not_duplicate_semantic_effects)
followup_transaction.semantic_uniqueness_concurrent: concurrent attempts to materialize the same already-decided followup (including attempts carrying different idempotency keys) produce at most one child semantic effect: exactly one attempt commits; every other attempt fails closed with REVISION_CONFLICT (parent CAS race) or TRANSACTION_CONFLICT (two-root atomicity); distinct-key contention is never collapsed into key-reuse conflict, and no duplicate child is ever created

multi_parent_followup_policy.canonical_shape: the canonical M3-A3 parent -> new-child transaction is exactly ONE existing parent Subject plus a new child Subject
multi_parent_followup_policy.rule: a child that requires multiple EXISTING parents is deferred/denied as a cross-existing-Subject transaction: it is not a canonical A3 transaction, it commits nothing in A3 scope, and it produces no child/edge partial effect
multi_parent_followup_policy.no_silent_reduction: a multi-parent intent must never be silently reduced to one parent: either the explicit multi-parent transaction is authorized by the deferred lane or the operation fails closed; there is no silent parent loss
multi_parent_followup_policy.future_rule: if a multi-parent followup is later authorized, the future transaction must CAS ALL participating parent aggregates (each with its expected revision) and commit child + all edges atomically; this is an explicit defer, not an implementation

edge_ownership_boundary.edge_is_cross_root_lineage_record: a FollowupEdge is a cross-root lineage record (A1: parenthood defined only by edges), not dual authoritative ownership: it never grants authority to either root and no root 'owns' the other through the edge
edge_ownership_boundary.edge_creation_owner: parent CAS and parent revision own edge creation: the edge commits as part of the parent aggregate's revision advance (outgoing edge) in the followup transaction
edge_ownership_boundary.child_lineage_snapshot: the child's initial revision includes the committed lineage snapshot (its incoming parent edge(s) and source Decision reference) as immutable record content
edge_ownership_boundary.no_independent_edge_revision: there is no independent edge revision: edges are append-only, fixed at creation, and carry no revision counter or token of their own
edge_ownership_boundary.no_dual_authority: edge participation in two roots' records never creates dual authoritative ownership: both roots' revisions advance as one atomic unit, and DUAL_AUTHORITATIVE_WRITE=no is preserved

followup_transaction.no_heuristic_parent: parent selection is never heuristic (A1 NO_HEURISTIC_PARENT_SELECTION=yes); the edge carries the explicit parent reference from the materialized decision

multi_subject_policy.default: one authoritative transaction touches exactly one Subject aggregate; independent Subjects are never serialized by default
multi_subject_policy.global_serialization_rule: a single global process mutex is NOT canonical and is never the default concurrency mechanism; independent Subjects must be concurrently mutable via per-aggregate CAS
multi_subject_policy.explicit_serialization_allowed: explicit, documented, bounded serialization is acceptable ONLY where CAS cannot express the required invariant (e.g., a defined two-root protocol or an explicitly scoped counter); every such use must state its scope and justification
multi_subject_policy.canonical_two_root: parent -> new-child followup creation is the only canonical cross-Subject transaction in A3 scope; it is safe because the child does not pre-exist, so only the parent side can race (parent CAS governs the commit)
deferred_cross_subject: attaching an ADDITIONAL parent edge to an existing child (multi-parent on an existing Subject)
a followup child requiring multiple EXISTING parents at creation (multi-parent followup; MULTI_PARENT_FOLLOWUP_DEFERRED=yes - must CAS all participating parent aggregates if later authorized)
any other mutation spanning two pre-existing Subject aggregates
cross-Subject reference updates beyond followup creation
multi_subject_policy.deferred_rule: cross-existing-Subject transactions are minimized and deferred: their semantics contract (atomicity, CAS ordering, idempotency, conflict behavior) follows this artifact, but no authoritative operation defines them in A3 scope and no implementation exists
multi_subject_policy.justification_section: any future explicit serialization must be recorded in this policy with scope + reason; silent global serialization is a contract violation

concurrency_rules.independent_subjects: independent Subject aggregates mutate concurrently; each commit CASes its own aggregate revision token; no global lock, no whole-graph revision
concurrency_rules.same_aggregate: concurrent mutations of the same aggregate: exactly one commits (expected == current); every other requester receives REVISION_CONFLICT and must re-validate with fresh facts; no merging and no silent overwrite of a committed update
concurrency_rules.read_path: reads (projections, diagnostics) are never blocked by mutation; they may observe a pre-commit or post-commit snapshot, never a partial authoritative transition
concurrency_rules.retry_policy: retry is allowed only after fresh validation: new lease with the new expected revision, new authority evaluation, re-verified semantic basis; blind replay with stale facts is denied
concurrency_rules.ordering_guarantee: within one aggregate, committed revisions are totally ordered by revision_number; across aggregates, no global ordering exists and none is needed

idempotency_model.scope: authoritative bounded mutations of Subject aggregates, including the followup transaction; read-only projections and diagnostics are outside idempotency scope

content.idempotency_key_binding: principal/authority context + operation (contract identity) + typed target (object_kind + object_id + expected revision context) + semantic fingerprint
content.semantic_fingerprint: deterministic digest of the semantic payload of the request (for followup: the source Decision reference + statement + target references; for transitions: the requested transition + evidence references)
content.key_rule: the key binds actor and operation and target so that a different principal, different operation, or different target can never consume the same dedupe slot

request_vs_semantic_effect.request_dedupe: the request layer returns the recorded outcome for an identical request without re-executing (replay protection at the request boundary)
request_vs_semantic_effect.semantic_effect_dedupe: the durable effect layer guarantees that a replay can never duplicate a semantic effect: a child Subject is created at most once, a mechanical transition applies at most once, a Completion records at most once; the two layers are distinct and both required

idempotency_model.retention: idempotency records are retained at least until the committed outcome is fully derivable from the durable record set and downstream projection/audit consumption is complete; the exact retention duration and storage are M3-B implementation
idempotency_model.replay: replay with the same key and same semantic fingerprint returns the previously recorded outcome and creates no new semantic effect
idempotency_model.mismatch: the same idempotency key with a different payload/fingerprint is REJECTED with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; it is never silently overwritten and never silently reused (same key/different payload is a contract violation)
idempotency_model.duplicate_effect_denied: a duplicate child Subject, duplicate Completion, or duplicate transition caused by replay is a design violation: IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY=must_not_duplicate_semantic_effects

conflicts.meaning: CAS pre-commit check failed: expected revision token != current revision token of the target aggregate (a concurrent committed mutation won)
conflicts.notes: the core concurrency conflict; stale mutation fails closed; no merge, no last-write-wins

conflicts.meaning: an idempotency key was reused with a different payload/fingerprint, or with a different bound principal/operation/target
conflicts.notes: same key/different payload is rejected; resolution requires explicit semantic choice, never silent overwrite

conflicts.meaning: the requested mechanical transition is invalid from the Subject's current mechanical state (e.g., PROPOSED->ACTIVE from COMPLETED), independent of any revision race
conflicts.notes: state-machine validity, distinct from concurrency: revision conflicts are about timing, predecessor conflicts are about legality of the transition

conflicts.meaning: the authority facts were valid at issuance but stale at consumption: unexpired lease whose expected_revision no longer equals the current target revision, or a lease/principal binding invalidated since issuance
conflicts.notes: staleness is a hard denial even when the lease has not expired (STALE_UNEXPIRED_LEASE_DENIED=yes); a fresh lease through issuance rules is required

conflicts.meaning: a multi-root (followup) transaction could not commit atomically: e.g., the parent CAS failed after the child side was prepared
conflicts.notes: no partial authoritative transition is ever visible; the whole transaction reports the conflict; replay is idempotency-protected

crash_atomicity.commit_atomicity: the authoritative transaction is atomic: observers never see a partial authoritative transition (no child without edge, no edge without child, no half-applied mechanical transition)
crash_atomicity.crash_before_commit: nothing of the transaction is durable and nothing is visible; retry is safe and idempotency-protected
crash_atomicity.crash_after_commit: the full commit unit is durable and visible; projections and audit are rebuildable from the durable record set; no second application (idempotency)
crash_atomicity.crash_during_commit: the outcome is exactly committed-or-not: an atomic commit primitive is required at implementation time (M3-B); the design freezes that no intermediate state is observable
crash_atomicity.recovery_relation: recovery (M4 lane) reconciles from durable records; the durable record set plus idempotency records are sufficient to detect and complete or reject uncertain operations; no hidden intermediate state is representable
crash_atomicity.no_dual_write: projection and audit writes are post-commit and never part of the atomicity unit

projection_relation.definition: projections (current decision per kind, current plan selection, current followup, binding 0/1/many) are derived deterministically from the committed durable record set after the authoritative commit
projection_relation.projection_failure_dual_authority_ration: projections are never competing authority: they are derived, rebuildable read-models over the committed durable record set (CURRENT_POINTERS_ARE_PROJECTIONS=yes) and can never become a second authoritative write; a projection failure therefore leaves the durable record set as the sole authority and never creates a dual authoritative source (DUAL_AUTHORITATIVE_WRITE=no preserved)
projection_relation.projection_lag: permitted: a projection may lag the authoritative commit, but it can never add authority and never binds a wrong subject (stale pointer state cannot hide or substitute a durable Subject)
projection_relation.rebuildable: projections are rebuildable from durable records alone (A1 CURRENT_POINTERS_ARE_PROJECTIONS=yes)
projection_relation.fail_closed: ambiguous projections return NEEDS_SEMANTIC_CHOICE (SUBJECT_BINDING_ZERO_ONE_MANY; A5 lane)

audit_relation.definition: the canonical audit record captures, per authoritative transaction: bound principal (A2 design requirement AUDIT_RECORDS_PRINCIPAL=required_design), operation, typed target, expected and resulting revision, outcome, and idempotency key
audit_relation.audit_character: audit is a diagnostic/provenance trace, never graph authority: it records what happened after the fact and participates in no authoritative state, no projection, and no selection (EVENT_LOG_IS_SUBJECT_AUTHORITY=no)
audit_relation.after_commit: audit is written after the authoritative commit and is evidence, never a second authoritative write (DUAL_AUTHORITATIVE_WRITE=no)
audit_relation.audit_repair: audit records are reconstructible from the durable record set; missing audit does not corrupt the authoritative graph state

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: stale writer rejected after concurrent commit
concurrency_scenarios.given: Subject S at revision 4; writers A and B both read revision 4
concurrency_scenarios.when: A commits first (S advances to revision 5); B then attempts its commit with expected revision 4
concurrency_scenarios.expected: B is rejected with REVISION_CONFLICT (STALE_REVISION_MUTATION=fail_closed); nothing is written by B; no lost update and no silent last-write-wins; B must re-read revision 5 and re-validate with fresh facts before retry

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: independent Subjects succeed without global serialization
concurrency_scenarios.given: two different Subject aggregates S1 and S2, each with valid unexpired leases at their correct expected revisions
concurrency_scenarios.when: two agents mutate S1 and S2 concurrently
concurrency_scenarios.expected: both commits succeed via per-aggregate CAS; no global serialization, no global lock, no whole-graph revision; S1 and S2 revisions advance independently

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: two otherwise-valid writers on the same Subject/revision
concurrency_scenarios.given: Subject S at revision R; two writers A and B, both otherwise valid (fresh leases, expected revision R, authority facts satisfied)
concurrency_scenarios.when: A and B attempt their mutations concurrently against the same expected revision R
concurrency_scenarios.expected: exactly one CAS succeeds and S advances; the other receives a deterministic REVISION_CONFLICT; no merge, no silent last-write-wins, no lost update; the loser must re-validate with fresh facts

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: stale unexpired lease denied on revision mismatch
concurrency_scenarios.given: Subject S at revision 7 when lease L is issued with expected_revision 7; the target advances to revision 8 before consumption
concurrency_scenarios.when: the holder presents the still-unexpired lease L to mutate S
concurrency_scenarios.expected: denied due to revision mismatch (revision 7 -> revision 8; REVISION_MISMATCH / AUTHORITY_STALE; STALE_LEASE_REVISION_MUTATION=denied); the unexpired lease cannot mutate the moved target and lease expiry cannot silently expand authority; LEASE_REISSUE_REQUIRED_AFTER_REVISION_CHANGE=yes (a fresh lease with expected_revision 8 must be issued)

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: lost response retry with same idempotency key
concurrency_scenarios.given: a mutation committed but the client lost the response; the durable idempotency record holds the outcome
concurrency_scenarios.when: the client retries the same request with the same idempotency key and same semantic fingerprint
concurrency_scenarios.expected: the same idempotency key returns the same recorded result (returned or reconstructed deterministically); no semantic effect is duplicated (no second child, no second transition, no second Completion); IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY=must_not_duplicate_semantic_effects

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: same idempotency key with different semantic payload
concurrency_scenarios.given: idempotency key K was already used for semantic payload P1
concurrency_scenarios.when: the same key K is presented with a different semantic payload P2
concurrency_scenarios.expected: fails closed with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; the payload is never silently overwritten and the key is never silently reused; resolution requires an explicit semantic choice

concurrency_scenarios.NAME: concurrent materialization of the same decided followup
concurrency_scenarios.given: an already-decided followup (materialized Decision D) on parent Subject P; two agents attempt to materialize it concurrently, possibly with different idempotency keys
concurrency_scenarios.when: both attempts reach the followup transaction commit path
concurrency_scenarios.expected: at most one child semantic effect is created even across attempts with different idempotency keys: exactly one attempt commits (parent CAS + edge + child initial revision); every other attempt fails closed with REVISION_CONFLICT (parent CAS race) or TRANSACTION_CONFLICT (two-root atomicity); because the competing attempts carry different idempotency keys, this is distinct-key contention, not key reuse, so IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT is not the loser outcome for this case; no duplicate child ever exists; crash atomicity is covered by crash_atomicity, not by this scenario
